ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Booker T. Washington

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for low back pain

text.paragraph: Low back pain for three days after lifting. [S]

Mr. Washington is a 59-year-old man with hypertensive chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (eGFR 30 in June), controlled on amlodipine, losartan, dapagliflozin, and chlorthalidone, who asked for a same-day visit. Three days ago, while loading heavy boxes of books into a car before a speaking trip, he felt a sudden pull across the right lower back. The pain is a deep ache, worse on bending, twisting, and getting out of a chair, and it eases when he lies on his side or walks slowly. It does not travel below the buttock. He has no numbness, tingling, or leg weakness, no change in bladder or bowel control, no numbness in the groin or saddle area, and no fever or weight loss. He has never had cancer. Before the visit he took over-the-counter naproxen, two 220 mg tablets twice a day for two days, then remembered that his care plan says to avoid these medicines and stopped yesterday. He has had no vomiting or diarrhea and is eating and drinking normally. Sitting through a long car ride yesterday made the pain worse. [S]

Strain of muscle, fascia and tendon of lower back, initial encounter

list.item:
Acute lumbar muscle strain (S39.012A). Mechanical low back pain after lifting, with a normal neurological examination and no red flags such as fever, cancer history, weight loss, saddle numbness, or bladder or bowel change. Imaging and laboratory tests for the back are not indicated. Most episodes improve within a few weeks. [S]
Superficial heat for 20 minutes several times a day.
Stay active within the limits of pain and avoid bed rest; stand and walk for a few minutes every hour when traveling.
Acetaminophen 1 g up to three times a day as needed, no more than 3 g a day.
No naproxen, ibuprofen, or other oral NSAIDs, including combination cold and pain products that contain them; a muscle relaxant was discussed and not started because of sedation while he travels.
Physical therapy referral if the pain is not clearly better in two to four weeks.

Chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (N18.32). Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL and eGFR 30, the same as in June, and potassium 4.7 mmol/L, so two days of naproxen caused no measurable harm. NSAIDs taken with losartan, a diuretic, and an SGLT2 inhibitor can cause acute kidney injury, and the combination is the main risk in this visit. [S]
NSAIDs recorded in his chart as medicines to avoid, and his pharmacy asked to flag them.
Reviewed the sick-day rule: hold dapagliflozin, losartan, and chlorthalidone on any day with vomiting, diarrhea, or poor fluid intake, and call.
Continue current doses; kidney tests as planned at the October review.

Severe hypertension with hypertensive kidney disease (I12.9). Blood pressure 132/82 mmHg, above his recent readings, likely from pain and the NSAID. [S]
No change; recheck at the preventive visit next month and continue home readings.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024); Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2017)

Follow-up: Return or call for leg weakness or numbness, numbness in the groin, loss of bladder or bowel control, fever, or pain that is not improving in two to four weeks. Preventive visit next month. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-21: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
